name: m365
summary: Microsoft 365 through Microsoft's Work IQ MCP server: mail, calendar, files, Teams (Entra sign-in, your own app registration)

connect.description: Microsoft 365 (Work IQ hosted MCP, Entra sign-in)

notes: Work-system caution: a Microsoft 365 tenant is usually a workplace system. Connect it only in a gateway zone the owner has approved for that tenant.
Before setup: a tenant administrator must enable Work IQ, and the delegated permission WorkIQAgent.Ask needs admin consent. Licensing and billing are Microsoft's: read the overview page.

Create the app in Entra (App registrations, New registration): supported account types 'Accounts in any organizational directory' (the server's sign-in authority is /organizations, which a single-tenant app cannot use); platform 'Mobile and desktop applications' with redirect URI http://localhost:8977/callback; allow public client flows; add the API permission WorkIQAgent.Ask from api://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft. No client secret.
lotr setup m365 then asks for the app's client id as a reference (store:m365-client-id; put it there with lotr secret put m365-client-id) and runs the sign-in in YOUR terminal.
Entra issues the token for api://workiq.svc.cloud.microsoft, not for the MCP URL, so the audience check is off and the resource parameter is not sent (Entra v2 refuses it).

Tiers: the server has generic tools. do_action can send mail, forward and move; create_entity can send a Teams message or an invitation; so do_action and the create / update / delete tools are consent. fetch, call_function (Graph functions only read), retrieve and the schema tools are reads. ask (Microsoft 365 Copilot) stays a write. Tenant policy blocks mutations by default as well.
Microsoft's per-workload Mail, Calendar and Teams MCP servers are a legacy preview that Microsoft says not to use for new work; this template uses Work IQ.
This is an alternative to the built-in REST connection (profile graph), which keeps working.
